_meta.notes: sev arrays give effective spoiler severity by player progress (index = milestone). Must be non-increasing. All items are DRAFT: derived from Game8, Sportskeeda, PowerPyx, Keengamer, GamerGuides and a Steam community guide (Sept 2026); impact and severity values are provisional and need human plus second-model audit.
_meta.scope: MVP slice: items obtainable in the Prologue or Act 1

items.title_safe: A respec tool from the starting area

t1.text: Talk to the artists in the market area before you leave the opening section.

t2.text: One market NPC gives you a tool that lets you reallocate attributes and skill points. It cannot be obtained later.

t3.text: Recoat: interact with the painter Nicholas at the Flower Market.

sources.name: Game8
sources.claim: Prologue, Flower Market, permanent

sources.name: Sportskeeda
sources.claim: Prologue, interact with Nicholas, permanent

sources.name: Steam guide 3469875590
sources.claim: Nicholas the Painter Duel: Recoat lost (farmable later)

items.conflict: Game8 and Sportskeeda call it permanent; the Steam guide says the Recoat lost from the painter duel is farmable later.

items.title_safe: A weapon upgrade material in the starting area

t1.text: Check odd corners of the market area, not only the main path.

t2.text: A weapon upgrade item is hidden near the stairs in the same area as the painter.

t3.text: Chroma Catalyst: search the trash can near the stairs by the painter Nicholas.

sources.name: Game8
sources.claim: Prologue, trash can, permanent

sources.name: Sportskeeda

sources.name: Steam guide 3469875590

t2.text: An outfit unlock is handed out by a festival NPC and is only available in the opening section.

items.title_safe: A hairstyle from a festival stall

t1.text: Festival stalls trade for something; do not skip them.

t1.text: Do not spend all your festival tokens on one stall.

t2.text: A key item from a stall unlocks a room and a journal entry in the old part of the city.

items.title_safe: An outfit quest in an early village

t1.text: Talk to every villager you meet in Act 1 before moving on.

t2.text: A small side quest in an early village rewards a special outfit for the lead character.

items.title_safe: A skill tied to a journal in your camp

t1.text: Read and interact with things at camp, not only fight.

t2.text: A skill unlock is tied to the camp journal and stops being available late in the game.

sources.claim: Act 1-2, camp journal, unavailable in Act 3

items.title_safe: An enemy type that is best left alone

t1.text: Some fights have consequences beyond the fight. Think before attacking every enemy you see.

t2.text: Attacking a certain harmless-looking enemy type turns a friendly NPC hostile and costs you a reward.

t3.text: Killing White Nevrons makes the NPC Blanche hostile and you lose 100 Colours of Lumina.

items.title_safe: A strong weapon from an arena fight

t1.text: Not every Act 1 reward is in a chest. Watch for organized fights in the first big hub town.

t2.text: An arena in the first hub town gives one party member a top weapon that stays useful for a long time. One guide says no replacement is available until very late.

t3.text: Medalum: win the Gestral Village tournament using Maelle (Keengamer: defeat Sel in the arena).

sources.name: Steam guide 3469875590
sources.claim: Win Gestral Village tournament with Maelle: Medalum; no other until late Act 3

sources.name: Keengamer early weapons
sources.claim: Gestral Village Arena, defeat Sel: Medalum

sources.claim: Medalum is best for Maelle in Acts 2-3

items.title_safe: An early Lune weapon from a strong optional enemy

t1.text: Strong-looking early enemies can carry gear worth the fight.

t2.text: An early weapon for Lune drops from a stronger 'Chromatic' enemy in the first open area and makes fire skills cheaper.

t3.text: Sakaram: drop from Robust Sakapatate in the Ancient Sanctuary.

t2.text: An early Lune weapon from the ruins generates elemental stains on attacks and refunds AP.

items.title_safe: An early weapon for Maelle from a fire enemy

t1.text: Enemy types matter: some carry gear specific to a party member.

t2.text: A crit-focused weapon for Maelle drops from a fire enemy in an early water-themed area.

t3.text: Brulerum: drop from a Bruler in Flying Waters.

t1.text: Save your currency for one big purchase at a station.

t2.text: A picto sold for a very large Chroma amount lets you survive one lethal hit per battle.

sources.name: Game8 best pictos

items.title_safe: A picto that lets you act first

t1.text: Look inside odd structures in early areas.

t2.text: A picto lets you act first so you can set up buffs before the enemy.

items.title_safe: A picto for extra break damage

t1.text: Tough optional enemies in the first ruins drop good pictos.

t2.text: A picto from a tough enemy gives a flat 25% boost to break damage.

t3.text: Breaker: defeat Ultimate Sakapatate in the Ancient Sanctuary.

sources.name: Game8 best pictos
sources.claim: Breaker: defeat Ultimate Sakapatate, Ancient Sanctuary

items.title_safe: The last Nevron request remembers how you treated others

t2.text: The final Nevron request pays a large Lumina reward if you spared the earlier Nevrons and much less if you did not.

sources.claim: Hexga, Stone Wave Cliffs: Auto Shell; collect three Rock Crystals

sources.claim: Bourgeon, The Small Bourgeon: Colour of Lumina; needs Bourgeon Skin

t1.text: Big-ticket purchases are coming. Do not spend all your currency early.

items.title_safe: Swimsuits from beach minigames

t1.text: The beach area has mini-games that reward outfits.

t2.text: Several party members get swimsuits from different beach mini-games, some with hard requirements.

t3.text: Gestral Beach: Gustave (parkour), Lune (question, or volleyball on Normal), Maelle (rock climbing), Sciel (volleyball Strongest), Monoco (Ascension).

sources.claim: Swimsuits from Gestral Beach parkour, volleyball, rock climbing, ascension

items.title_safe: Hairstyles and outfits from roaming Mime enemies

t1.text: Odd-looking enemies out in the world carry cosmetics.

t2.text: Mimes are optional enemies found across the map; defeating each awards a hairstyle or outfit.

t3.text: Examples: Baguette outfit/haircut (Spring Meadows), Bald haircut for each character (Sunless Cliffs), Braid (Old Lumiere), Sirene haircut (Sirene).

sources.claim: Mimes across many areas award haircuts and Baguette outfits

items.review_notes: Many locations; list is examples only. Single source.

items.title_safe: Lost Gestrals in the early areas

t1.text: Small Gestral characters hide across the first areas.

t2.text: Finding lost Gestrals and telling their leader gives haircuts and an ability. Some need a later traversal ability.

t3.text: 1 Esquie's Nest (Maelle haircut), 2 Stone Wave Cliffs (Lune haircut), 3 White Tree (Sciel haircut, needs swimming), 4 Monoco's Station (Paint Break), 5 Coastal Cave (Verso haircut, needs swimming).

items.title_safe: Festival stalls where you cannot buy everything

t1.text: You cannot have everything from the festival stalls.

t2.text: Festival Tokens are limited, so you pick which stall trade you want: a hairstyle, a key item or a picto item.

sources.claim: Festival Tokens: need 3 but can only get 1; if not Old Key, miss Connoisseur record

items.title_safe: A trophy that must be earned with your starting character

t1.text: Some combat trophies are tied to your starting character and must be earned early.

t1.text: A trophy needs a boss fight where you take no damage. Save an easy boss for it.

t2.text: Do not use up every chance: skip a particular early elite boss and return once you are strong enough.
